symptom: A Custom chart's eventDataAttribute bound to an attribute of another page parameter ($Ctx) inside a data view over $Entry had no spelling that built: `eventDataAttribute: $Ctx.EventData` was MDL-WIDGET42 "is a attribute property and cannot hold the expression $Ctx.EventData"; the qualified `MyFirstModule.ChartContext.EventData` passed check and exec and mx check said CE7247 "Attribute 'MyFirstModule.ChartContext.EventData' is not an attribute of entity 'MyFirstModule.ChartEntry'"; DESCRIBE of the Studio Pro-authored binding printed the qualified name, re-executing into the CE7247 shape.
cause: A generic pluggable key's value goes through the expression grammar, so `$Ctx.EventData` arrives as *ast.WidgetExpressionV3 and scalarPropertyText refused every expression on a non-Expression property; the engine's `$Param.Attr` -> AttributeRef + SourceVariable path existed only for mapped keys. The explicit-key pass stored any name with two dots as written, and misboundAttributeError skipped every qualified name. The first #1591 fix made describe print the qualified name back faithfully, which pinned the CE7247 shape in the bug-test MDL.
fix: `$Param.Attr` (strict shape: one variable, one attribute name) is accepted on attribute properties by exec and check, mapped or authored by key, and written as AttributeRef + Forms$PageVariable{PageParameter/SnippetParameter}; check also lets it through on a key whose kind is unknown (no project), since it is no Mendix expression. A qualified attribute whose entity is not the bound entity or a generalization of it is refused by the shared misboundAttributeError (check and exec, word for word), naming CE7247 and `$Param.Attr`. The generic pluggable describer prints a parameter-sourced attribute as `$Param.Attr`. mx check 11.12.5: 0 errors; describe -> exec round trip: Unchanged.
insight: A describe fix that makes the output 'faithful' to a stored shape is only half the question: run mx check on the shape it re-creates. Here the qualified name round-tripped byte for byte and still did not build, because what Studio Pro stores for the binding is a pair (AttributeRef + SourceVariable) and MDL had a spelling for the pair only on mapped keys. Wrong turn to skip: tightening the scope check alone would have left the reporter with no spelling at all; the refusal needs the spelling it points at. namedObjectBinding accepts `$Ctx.Name + 'x'` (it only cuts at the first dot), so the expression/attribute decision needs a strict shape test; the control expression case in the test caught it.
